title: Spend Sentinel — Usage & Billing Diagnostic Notebook
body:
Purpose:
This notebook is a compact, tactical worksheet for Customer Success and FinOps to use during QBR preparation and on-call triage. It focuses on token spend patterns, rate-limit interactions, and budget-alert tuning — with concrete queries, diagnostic steps, and a short escalation playbook teams can copy into a customer QBR packet.

Quick snapshot (fill in before the QBR):
- Customer: ____________________
- Contract tier: _______ (hosted / dedicated / private)
- Monthly committed spend: $______
- Current month tokens consumed: ______ tokens
- 30d avg tokens/day: _____
- 30d p95 concurrency (requests/min): _____
- Main routes used (top 3): 1) /v1/complete 2) /v1/chat 3) /v1/embed
- Primary cost driver (select): model size / token length / call volume / experimental loop / customer-side caching gap

Key metrics to collect (data sources shown):
- Tokens by route (billing.events, telemetry.requests) — p50/p95/p99 per-hour
- Token cost per model (billing.unit_costs) — include quantized variants
- Failed requests due to RateLimitExceeded (telemetry.errors) — include HTTP code and retry-after headers
- Budget burn rate (billing.daily_spend) — compare to committed spend runway
- Cache hit rate (serving.cache_metrics) — prefix cache effectiveness

Sample SQL / BigQuery snippets to run (adjust dataset names):
- Tokens by route (last 30d):
  SELECT route, DATE(timestamp) as day, SUM(tokens) as tokens
  FROM telemetry.requests
  WHERE customer_id = '<<CUSTOMER_ID>>' AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  GROUP BY route, day ORDER BY day DESC;

- Rate-limit failures aggregate (7d):
  SELECT route, error_code, COUNT(1) as failures
  FROM telemetry.errors
  WHERE customer_id = '<<CUSTOMER_ID>>' AND error_code = 'RateLimitExceeded' AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
  GROUP BY route, error_code ORDER BY failures DESC;

- 95th token-per-minute (burst) estimate (14d):
  SELECT DATE_TRUNC(timestamp, MINUTE) as minute_bucket, SUM(tokens) as tokens_min
  FROM telemetry.requests
  WHERE customer_id = '<<CUSTOMER_ID>>' AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 14 DAY)
  GROUP BY minute_bucket ORDER BY tokens_min DESC LIMIT 100;

Interpreting diagnostics (how to read the outputs):
- If tokens concentrate in a single route: ask product/engineering which frontend loop is creating those calls and whether batching or client-side caching is possible.
- If p95 tokens/min >> average tokens/min -> "token velocity" spikes indicate burst tax risk. Consider per-route rate caps or request shaping.
- If RateLimitExceeded aligns with deploy times: this is a capacity spike; treat as "traffic event" vs. behavioral pattern.
- If token cost per call is high due to model variant: propose switching to a lower-cost quantized variant for background workloads and reserve the high-cost model for interactive endpoints.

Budget alert tuning patterns (recommended defaults — tweak per customer):
- Alert A (Early Warning): daily burn > 3x planned daily average for 3 consecutive days -> notify CSM and FinOps (email + slack)
- Alert B (Throttle Warning): p95 tokens/min exceeds reserved headroom by 20% for >10 minutes -> create incident in PagerDuty (severity P3) and notify solutions-eng
- Alert C (Commit Risk): projected end-of-month spend at current burn > committed + 10% -> escalate to renewals lead and AM
- Alert D (Unexpected model change): sudden change (>50%) in model mix within 24h -> CS + APPLIED ML review (possible release misconfiguration)

Playbook: triage steps for a billing spike or rapid token burn
1) Validate data (5 min): run the 30d tokens-by-route and 95th-minute queries. Confirm spike window and top routes.
2) Classify cause (10 min): code deploy? customer experiment? scheduled job? model swap? Use linked GitHub PRs or release notes.
3) Contain (15 min): if immediate cost risk, apply one of: temporary per-route rate cap (CS console), throttle to quantized model, or enable prefix cache for repeated prompts. Document the change and TTL.
4) Communicate (ongoing): send a short incident note to customer with current mitigation and next steps. Update the QBR ticket.
5) Follow-up (3 days): propose a durable fix (client SDK update, model routing rule, reserved capacity increase, or a discount review) and log action item with owner and ETA.

QBR agenda snippet to include in customer packet:
- 5m: Hey/updates
- 10m: Usage snapshot & top-line spend trend (include chart)
- 10m: Risk highlights (alerts triggered, burst events, failed requests)
- 10m: Cost optimization recommendations (batching, model variants, caching)
- 10m: Action items / next steps (owner + dates)

Common mitigation templates (copy into a customer note):
- Short-term: "We temporarily applied a 25% per-route cap on /v1/complete for 6 hours to stop the immediate burn while we investigate. This will be reverted at HH:MM unless further actions are required."
- Medium-term: "We recommend routing background scoring to model-x-quantized (estimated 45% token-cost reduction) and enabling a 12-hour cache for repeated prompts. Estimated monthly savings: $X."
- Long-term: "Consider a dedicated capacity commit if 30d average sustained tokens/day > X and p95 concurrency > Y. This reduces unit cost and provides headroom without emergency throttling."

Escalation matrix (who to ping):
- CSM: primary contact (Slack + email)
- FinOps: for billing projection deviations > 10%
- Solutions Eng: if routing or SDK changes required
- Applied ML: if model mix changes are suspected

Action item template to add to QBR notes (copy/paste):
- Action: _______________________
- Owner: _______________________
- Due: _________________________
- Status: todo / in_progress / done
- Notes: _______________________
